auxiliary_passages.statement_original: For a function $f:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R$, we define $\boldsymbol f=(f(\boldsymbol x_1),\ldots,f(\boldsymbol x_n))^\top$ to be the $n\times1$ vector of $f$ evaluated at the design points $\boldsymbol X=(\boldsymbol x_1,\ldots,\boldsymbol x_n)^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$. Likewise, we use $\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}(T_K)$ to denote the $n\times1$ vector of fitted values of $\widehat\mu(T_K)$. For functions $f,g\in\mathcal L_2(P_{\boldsymbol x})$, let $\|f\|^2=\int_{\mathcal X}(f(\boldsymbol x))^2dP_{\boldsymbol x}(\boldsymbol x)$ be the squared $\mathcal L_2(P_{\boldsymbol x})$ norm and let $\|\boldsymbol f\|_n^2=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(f(\boldsymbol x_i))^2$ denote the squared norm with respect to the empirical measure on the data. Let $\langle\boldsymbol f,\boldsymbol g\rangle_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nf(\boldsymbol x_i)g(\boldsymbol x_i)$ denote the inner product with respect to the empirical measure on the data. The response data vector $\boldsymbol y=(y_1,\ldots,y_n)^\top\in\mathbb R^n$ is viewed as a relation, defined on the design matrix $\boldsymbol X$, that associates $\boldsymbol x_i$ with $y_i$. Thus, for example, $\|\boldsymbol y-\boldsymbol f\|_n^2=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(y_i-f(\boldsymbol x_i))^2$ and $\langle\boldsymbol y,\boldsymbol f\rangle_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^ny_if(\boldsymbol x_i)$. We use $[T]$ to denote the collection of internal (non-terminal) nodes and $\{t:t\in T\}$ to denote the terminal nodes of the tree. The cardinality of a set $A$ is denoted by $|A|$.

unresolved_source_conventions.detail: Section 2.1 prints h(x)=sum h_k(x), then sums V(h_k,a_k,t), with directions a_k not bound in that displayed expansion and the node t suppressed in the norm notation. The following relaxed norm uses ridge expansions explicitly. The source passages are kept intact. The dependency graph uses the finite-sum construction for the finite library before the closure/relaxed-norm construction; this is an interpretation of the source staging, not a claim that the notation is fully unambiguous.

The source calls these functionals norms. Constant functions have zero variation, so they are seminorms unless an additional quotient or normalization is intended. No such change is made to the source definitions. F is an L2 closure, and finite relaxed variation for every member is not explicitly asserted.
The text defines |A| as cardinality, but writes a partition P={z_0,...,z_|P|}, containing |P|+1 points. The sum and indexing are preserved rather than silently renumbered.

The projection interval uses min/max even though tree cells can be relatively open or unbounded. Infinite endpoints are explicitly allowed, but endpoint evaluation of h and finite unattained extrema are not given conventions. No replacement by infimum/supremum or truncation is inserted into the quotation.

The printed smallest-minimizer explanation says T_opt precedes every pruned subtree, without limiting the comparison to minimizing subtrees. The optimization definition and this wording are retained; the natural minimizing-subtrees interpretation is not substituted into the original.

The statement that collapsing a node decreases unpenalized empirical squared error conflicts with least-squares node means. This is not used as a replacement for the explicit penalized optimization defining T_opt.

Assumption 4 quantifies over every K>=1 with a fixed finite A at a given n. Under the printed finite-sample stopping rule, a nonempty sample always leaves a terminal node with at least one observation, whereas An/2^K tends to zero. Thus the literal unlimited-depth quantifier needs clarification if the same stopped tree family is used for arbitrarily large K. The source is not silently restricted to feasible depths.

Node means require nonempty children, but the displayed optimization permits all real b and all candidate directions. Candidate nonemptiness, tie selection, and empty-child handling are not explicitly specified. The source finite-values argument establishes attainment only once the criterion and admissible splits are defined.

A tree stopped at its root has no ordinary internal nodes. Section 2.3 adds a formal empty node for the orthogonal expansion, but does not specify a search set or split-success probability for it, nor explicitly state whether that augmentation applies to the oracle maximum. Thus either a maximum-over-empty convention or a formal-node probability convention needs clarification. Zero success probability also requires an extended-real reciprocal, possibly multiplied by zero variation. The separate non-vacuous integrability discussion does not impose Assumption 1 on Theorems 1 or 5.

Section 2.2 declares d to be a positive integer bounding the number of nonzero coordinates. It does not explicitly add d<=p, although choosing an effective bound no larger than p is natural. The logarithmic terms and tiny sample sizes also need boundary conventions (n=1 or N=1 can make complexity terms zero). These parameter restrictions are not invented.

The positive-constant statement for gamma is followed by the separate gamma=infinity convention for bounded responses. The meaning of B^infinity at boundary thresholds is not stated; the natural 4/gamma=0 interpretation of risk exponents is recorded separately.

The text states without-replacement subsampling and independent copies of Theta, with all trees sharing the original sample. Independence is therefore read conditionally on that sample. The subsampling law is not further specified in the defining paragraph; uniform selection independent of observed values is conventional but is not inserted into the source. The purely random candidate directions on page 8 are examples, not a unique prescribed law.

The paper announces broader finite-dimensional least-squares node fits under weak assumptions and refers to appendix generality. The inspected main text does not completely specify that generalized theorem version. The census preserves the canonical mean-output statements and archives the announcement without consulting appendices.

Random sample is read conventionally as i.i.d.; the defining sentence does not separately spell out independence. The source describes F as an L2 closure but evaluates ridge representatives pointwise to measure variation, without specifying an equivalence-class representative convention. No choice is silently added.

M is the number of terms in a finite ridge representation on page 5 and a separate positive tail-shift constant in Assumption 2; C in Theorems 1 and 4 depends on the latter. B is a tail threshold in Assumption 2 and separately the number of forest trees on page 16. These uses are scoped separately.
